questions.q_en: In a race, Anurag gives a lead of 90 m to Vipul. If Anurag runs 2 times as fast as Vipul, then find the distance Anurag has to run before they meet?
questions.solution_en:
If time of constant, then

Ratio of speed = Ratio of distance

Ratio of speed of Anurag and Vipul = 2:1

Ratio of distance = 2:1

So,

1 unit = 90 m

2 unit = 2*90 = 180 m

questions.q_en: Suresh is 1(2/7) time faster than Naresh. In a race, Suresh gives a head start of 50 m to Naresh. Find the length of the race if both finished the race at same time.
questions.solution_en:
Ratio of speed of Suresh and Naresh = 1(2/7) : 1 = 9:7

Let speed of Suresh and Naresh is 9X m/s and 7X m/s respectively.

Let distance covered by Naresh = L m

Since, both reach at the same time -

(L + 50)/9X = L/7X

7L + 350 = 9L

2L = 350

L = 175

The length of race = 175 + 50 = 225 m

questions.q_en: P gives Q a lead of 54 meters to end a race in dead heat. If P runs 30% faster than Q, then find the length of race course.

Ratio of speed = Ratio of distance

Ratio of distance = 13:10

Length of race = 54*13/(13 - 10) = 234 m

questions.q_en: Himanshu and Kapil takes 2 minutes 50 seconds and 3 minutes 20 seconds to complete a race respectively. If they both start the race from starting point at the same time, then Himanshu beats Kapil by 60 meters. What is the length of race course.
questions.solution_en:
Difference between time = 3 minutes 20 seconds - 2 minutes 50 seconds = 200 - 170 = 30 seconds

So, Kapil covers 60 meters in 30 seconds

Speed of Kapil = 2 m/s

Length of race course = 200*2 = 400 m

Difference between time = 160 - 150 = 10 seconds

Distance by which Pooja beats Preeti = 6.25 * 10 = 62.5 m

questions.q_en: In a race of 1440 m from point A to B, Deep reaches to point B in 1.5 minutes, while Reet reaches to point B in 96 seconds. By how much distance does Deep beats Reet?

Difference between time = 96 - 1.5 * 60 = 6 seconds

Distance by which Deep beats Reet = 6 * 15 = 90 m

questions.q_en: In a race of three oxen Heera, Moti and Ramu, Heera beats Moti by 12 metres and Ramu by 87 metres. If Moti beat Ramu by 76 metres, what was the length of the race course?
questions.solution_en:
Let the length of race course = L meters

Distance covered by Heera = L meters

Distance covered by Moti = 'L - 12' meters

Distance covered by Ramu = 'L - 87' meters

and

Distance covered by Moti = L meters

Distance covered by Ramu = 'L - 76' meters

Now,

(L - 12)/(L - 87) = L/(L - 76)

L2 - 88L + 912 = L2 - 87L

L = 912

Therefore, length of race course = 912 meters

questions.q_en: In a 300 meters race, X defeats Y by 20 meters and Y defeats Z by 15 meters. By what distance will X defeats Z in the same race?
questions.solution_en:
When X covers 300 => Y covers 300 - 20 = 280

When Y covers 300 => Z covers 300 - 15 = 285

X/Y = 300/280 = 15/14 and Y/Z = 300/285 = 20/19

X/Z = (15/14) * (20/19) = 300/266

X defeats Z in the same race by => 300 - 266 = 34 meters

questions.q_en: In a bike race, first bike beats second by 50 km, second bike beats third by 60 km and first bike beats third by 100 km. Find the length of race course where bike race is conducted.
questions.solution_en:
Since, time is constant,

Speed of bike = Distance travelled by bike

Let the length of race course = L meters

Speed of 1st bike/Speed of 2nd bike = L/(L - 50) ------(1)

Speed of 2nd bike/Speed of 3rd bike = L/(L - 60) ------(2)

Speed of 1st bike/Speed of 3rd bike = L/(L - 100) ------(3)

Eqn (1) * eqn(2) = eqn (3)

[L/(L - 50)] * [L/(L - 60)] = L/(L - 100)

L2 - 100L = L2 - 110L + 3000

10L = 3000

L = 300 km

questions.q_en: P can win Q by 100 m in a race of 900 m. What should be the change in distance of startup if Q covers 1/3rd less distance than that by P in the same time?
questions.solution_en:
Initially distance covered by P = 900 m

Distance covered by Q = 900 - 100 = 800 m

New distance covered by Q = 900 * (1 - 1/3) = 600

New startup = 800 - 600 = 200 m

questions.q_en: In a race, Rani beats Vani by 252 m or 36 seconds. If the speed of Rani is 10 m/s, then find the speed of Vani.
questions.solution_en:
Let the speed of Vani = X m/s and length of race course = L meters

Speed of Rani = 10 m/s

L/10 = (L - 252)/X

X = 10(L - 252)/L -------(1)

and

L/X - L/10 = 36

X = L/(36 + L/10) ------(2)

From equation (1) and (2)-

10(L - 252)/L = L/(36 + L/10)

(L - 252)(360 + L) = L2

108L = 252*360

L = 840

X = 840/(36 + 840/10)

X = 840/120

X = 7 m/s

Hence, the speed of Vani = 7 m/s

questions.q_en: Abhay runs 2.5 times as fast as Nikita. If Abhay allows Nikita a 75 meters head start, at what distance should the finish line be set so that both reach it simultaneously?

i.e. 5 - 2 = 3 metres is gained by Abhay in 5 meters.

75 m is gained by Abhay in (5/3) * 75 = 125 m

questions.q_en: In a race of 800 m, Ashu beats Nishu by 100 m and Nishu beats Rishu by 80 m. By how much distance does Ashu beat Rishu?
questions.solution_en:
Let the speeds of Ashu, Nishu and Rishu be X m/s, Y m/s and Z m/s respectively.

800/X = (800 - 100)/Y

800/X = 700/Y ----(1)

800/Y = (800 - 80)/Z

800/Y = 720/Z

700/Y = 720*700/800Z

700/Y = 630/Z -------(2)

From equation (1) and (2)-

800/X = 630/Z

Required distance = 800 - 630 = 170 m

questions.q_en: In a 1260 m race, Naman beats Pawan by 280 m or 40 seconds. Find the sum of the speed of Pawan and Naman.
questions.solution_en:
Let the speed of Naman and Pawan are X m/s and Y m/s respectively.

1260/X = (1260 - 280)/Y

1260/X = 980/Y

9/X = 7/Y -------(1)

1260/Y - 1260/X = 40

63/Y - 63/X = 2 ------(2)

From equation (1) and (2)-

63/Y - 49/X = 2

14/Y = 2

Y = 7 m/s

X = 9 m/s

Hence, the speed of Pawan and Naman = 7 + 9 = 16 m/s
